reviewNote: Lunara is unfinished and installs unsigned onto the reader's own phone. The guide says so before the first command.

setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Git responds with a version number

setupSteps.title: Install Node LTS
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Node responds with a version number

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.body: Keep it open beside Iris.
steps.verifierLabel: Terminal is open

steps.title: Check Git and Node
steps.body: Git and the current Node LTS are required.
steps.verifierLabel: Git and Node respond with version numbers

steps.title: Install pnpm
steps.body: Lunara is a pnpm workspace.
steps.verifierLabel: pnpm responds with a version number

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has `npm install -g pnpm` finished successfully — a line such as "added 1 package" or "changed 1 package", followed by a fresh shell prompt? Answer not done while it is still downloading, or if it stopped on a permissions error such as EACCES.

hints: If npm reported a permissions error, install Node from nodejs.org rather than working around it — that installer puts npm's global folder somewhere you own.
Once it finishes, close this terminal window and open a new one so the new command is on your PATH.

steps.title: Copy Lunara to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d lunara/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/lunara.git
fi
steps.verifierLabel: A lunara folder appears

steps.title: Open the lunara folder
steps.verifierLabel: Your terminal prompt is inside the lunara folder

steps.title: Use the reviewed version
steps.verifierLabel: Git reports the reviewed commit

expect.prompt: In the terminal, does the output of `git checkout` include the line "HEAD is now at 197f66b"? Answer not done if it shows an error such as "not a git repository" or "pathspec ... did not match".

hints: "not a git repository" means the `cd lunara` before this did not happen — run that first, then this again.
Git will also say you are in "detached HEAD" state. That is expected: it is what pinning to a reviewed commit looks like.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.body: Warnings — even red ones — are normal here. It only failed if the last line names an error.
steps.verifierLabel: The command finishes without an error

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has `pnpm install` finished — a summary such as "Done in 42s" or "Already up to date", followed by a fresh shell prompt? Answer not done while a progress line is still moving.

hints: "pnpm: command not found" means this window was opened before pnpm was installed. Close it, open a new one, `cd ~/lunara`, and run it again.
This is the longest wait so far on a first install. It is downloading, not stuck.

steps.title: Build the app bundle
steps.body: This also copies the bundle into the phone project.
steps.verifierLabel: The command ends with a sync summary

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has the Capacitor sync finished — several lines beginning with a ✔ (copy, update, sync) and a summary such as "Sync finished in 1.5s", followed by a fresh shell prompt?

hints: The type check runs first and prints nothing at all for a while. Silence here is normal.
If it stopped on a TypeScript error you are probably not on the reviewed commit — run the `git checkout` step again.

steps.title: Install Xcode
steps.body: Large — start it early. Open it once afterwards so it finishes installing.
steps.verifierLabel: Xcode opens without asking to finish setup

steps.title: Open the iPhone project
steps.verifierLabel: Xcode opens with the App project

expect.prompt: Is Xcode showing a project window for a project named "App" — a file navigator down the left and an editor beside it — rather than the "Welcome to Xcode" start window, a different project, or no Xcode window at all?

hints: This command rebuilds the web bundle before it opens Xcode, so there is a quiet wait first.
"cap: command not found" means the terminal is in the wrong folder, or `pnpm install` never finished.

steps.title: Sign the app with your Apple ID
steps.body: App target → Signing & Capabilities → Team. A free Apple ID works.
steps.verifierLabel: Signing & Capabilities shows no red error

expect.prompt: In Xcode's Signing & Capabilities pane for the App target, does the Team row show a team name rather than "None", with no red error text underneath it?

hints: No team in the list? Open the Team dropdown, choose "Add an Account…", and sign in with your Apple ID.
If it says the bundle identifier is unavailable, change it to something unique to you — app.lunara.mobile.yourname, say.

steps.title: Plug in your iPhone
steps.body: Unlock it, tap Trust, then pick it from the device menu.
steps.verifierLabel: Your iPhone is selected as the run destination

steps.title: Press Run
steps.body: The ▶ button. The first build takes a few minutes.
steps.verifierLabel: Xcode finishes with Build Succeeded

steps.title: Trust yourself on the iPhone
steps.body: On the phone: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → your Apple ID → Trust.
steps.verifierLabel: Your Apple ID shows as trusted

steps.title: Open Lunara on your iPhone
steps.body: A free signature lasts 7 days. Press Run again to renew it.
steps.verifierLabel: Lunara opens on your phone

unsupported.headline: A Windows PC cannot build an iPhone app
unsupported.reason: Apple only allows iPhone apps to be built and signed on macOS using Xcode, which Apple does not release for Windows. This is Apple's restriction, not a missing feature in Lunara or Iris — no setup, emulator, or virtual machine makes it work reliably.
alternatives: Borrow a Mac for about thirty minutes — the signature it installs lasts 7 days and can be renewed on any Mac.
Use an Android phone instead, which builds fine from Windows.
Run Lunara in your phone's browser from a computer on the same Wi-Fi. Your data still stays on the phone, but widgets, notifications, and Health integration are not available.
